description: Specific requirements of the post 16 hours per week Monday 8-1.30pm, and Friday 8-6.30pm Ability to use own judgement, resourcefulness and be able to work under pressure without direct supervision. To have excellent communication skills and patience. To be dependable and flexible. To observe strict confidentiality on all matters relating to the practice and its patients. Please see the job description for the main duties of the job. There is a comprehensive list found in this document. Specific requirements of the post Main duties and responsibilities Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the practice. Receive and route patients and visitors on arrival, always ensuring a friendly welcome. Answer the telephone quickly and efficiently in a polite manner. Follow Practice procedures and protocols accordingly. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Receive and make calls as required for Doctors, Nurses, other members of the Primary Health Care Team and the Practice Manager. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Record requests for home visits onto the computer, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Doctor-on-call. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient as per protocols. Prepare communication to patients regarding urgent/routine appointments and prescriptions with regards to letters, summaries, results etc received and follow-up appropriately. Open and distribute mail when required, ensuring that they are all date stamped. Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are followed. Ensure availability of stationery and /or other documents in both reception area and consulting rooms. Retrieve information from the computer as and when required. Enter patient information onto the computer as required. To include appropriate coding of all clinical information and correspondence. Patient notes and correspondence: o Retrieve and re-file records as required, ensuring strict alphabetical order is adhered to. o Ensure correspondence, reports, results etc are scanned promptly in the correct records in order that all correspondence is available when patients are seen. o Ensure records are kept in good repair with all necessary information on the outside cover clearly visible. Systematically record all patient activity within their computer records, e.g. DNA, cancelled appointment, telephone encounter etc. To initiate the surgery complaints procedure on receipt of a verbal or written complaint and inform the Complaints Manager. Ensure all forms requested are dealt with efficiently and the correct procedures followed. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-GMS) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Cover staff absence for sickness and holidays as set out in the contract of employment. Premises: - a. Open premises at the start of the day when first to arrive, de-activate alarm and make necessary preparations to receive patients. b. When last to leave at the end of the day, ensure that the building is totally secured, internal lights are off and the alarm activated following the closing routine protocol. c. Report any faults to the Operational Manager. In turn with other staff, make and serve refreshments, ensure the kitchen and waiting room is kept clean and tidy, ensure magazines, posters and all other health promotion material are current and appropriate. Undertake any other additional duties appropriate to the post as requested by the Partners, Practice Manager or the deputy or Reception Manager. Use any new and existing IT systems. Be prepared to respond to patients when they raise a query with a doctor. Take on any new training the Doctors may request, that may offer an improved service to our patients. Signpost Patients to different appointment in the Additional Roles via the Primary Care Network e.g. Clinical Pharmacist, Social Prescriber etc. Process or forward any emails received on the generic Manor Court email address. Help and support their colleagues throughout the surgery when needed. Confidentiality While seeking treatment, patients entrust us with or allow us to gather sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks. Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills. Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards. Reporting potential risks identified. Equality and Diversity The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers, and colleagues to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers, and colleagues. Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings, priorities, and rights. Personal/Professional Development The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility or maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development. Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Participation in one-to-one reviews. Quality The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Collaborate effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage own time, workload, and resources. Participate in raising and learning from adverse events. Communication The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members. Communicate effectively with patients and carers. Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards, and guidance. Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work. Participate in audit where appropriate.

title: Receptionist /Administrator
description: Rosemead Surgery is a friendly supportive practice . We are currently looking for a Receptionist /Administrator You will need to have a passion for helping people, and to be able to stay calm under pressure . Good communication skills will be an advantage as would previous experience of working in general practice and or other healthcare related environments. Experience of working with EMIS Clinical System will also be an advantage. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. The duties and responsibilities of the role are varied and can change from time to time with direction of the Assistant Practice Manager or Practice Manager. These will included maintaining and monitoring the practice appointment system. Processing requests for appointments , visits and telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate health care professional. Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines. JOB SUMMARY: It is the responsibility of each receptionist to assist in the smooth running of the Practice in general, and the reception area in particular, and to project a positive and friendly image to our patients and other professionals who may contact us either in person or via the telephone. To facilitate patients accessing the clinical care provided by the practice. To support the GPs and Nurses in providing that care. To act as first point of contact for anyone accessing the practice. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: To ensure that all visitors and telephone callers to the practice are greeted professionally. To ensure all telephone calls are managed appropriately. To manage the flow of patients arriving at the reception desk, for appointments, prescriptions, or queries. To ensure the clinical staffs receive medical records as requested. To ensure that repeat prescriptions are generated accurately and efficiently, within the 48 hours specified by the practice. KEY TASKS: Reception duties: Greeting and booking in or patients for surgeries and clinics. Dealing with patient enquiries efficiently and courteously. The receiving and recording of telephone messages taking appropriate action. Making appointments on EMIS Clinical System, by processing appointment requests for today, future appointments from patients in person and on the telephone. Ensure eConsults are processed daily and assigned appropriately. Ensure patients are signposted to relevant services, e.g. St Marks Hospital, local pharmacy, Social Prescriber, First Contract Physio etc Ensure all tasks are actioned and completed. Processing prescriptions repeats and filing for collection within 48 hours. Advising patients of relevant charges for private services Receiving specimens from patients ensuring all their details have been recorded whilst following Health & Safety policy. Tidying waiting room after surgery, ensuring premises are kept tidy between visits from the cleaning staff, tidy and sort magazines and leaflets, discarding old and damaged items as necessary. Administration duties: To have a thorough knowledge of all practice policies and procedures To work in accordance with written protocols Provide administrative support for clinical staff. Filing patient records and correspondence when necessary. Opening and distribution or practice post. Registering new patients following the Registration Protocol. Scanning of documents onto the medical system. All scanning should be cleared daily. To send letters to patients as necessary. Changing details on EMIS i.e. Change of address, telephone numbers etc. Other Information: Cover for other Reception team members for sickness and annual leave. Ensuring building security/premises at the end of the day and ensure the building is totally secured, internal lights off and alarm activated. To carry out any other duties agreed between employee and the practice to ensure the smooth running of the practice. Confidentiality: While seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, the Staff Handbook and the Practice Infection Control Policy, this will include: Using personal security systems with the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks. Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills. Keeping own work areas and general/patient areas free from hazards. Reporting potential risks identified. Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers, and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues. Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgemental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development. Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload, and resources Participate in audit where appropriate. Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members. Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. NHS Pension Scheme: The post holder will automatically be enrolled in the NHS Pension Scheme (subject to eligibility checks).

title: Administrator
description: We are looking for an Administrator to join our friendly and busy team at The Arch Medical Practice. This is an important role supporting the day-to-day running of the practice and helping us to deliver an efficient, high-quality service to our patients. The successful candidate will provide administrative support to the clinical and non-clinical teams, ensuring that patient information, correspondence and practice processes are managed accurately and efficiently. The role will involve a variety of administrative tasks, including handling incoming and outgoing correspondence, maintaining accurate patient records, processing information, supporting clinical workflows and responding to queries from colleagues and other healthcare professionals. You will play an important part in ensuring that the practice runs smoothly, supporting the wider team and helping to make sure that administrative processes are completed in a timely and organised manner. This is a varied and rewarding role for someone who is organised, reliable and has excellent attention to detail. You will need to be confident working in a busy environment, able to manage competing priorities and have good communication and IT skills. We are a large, supportive GP training practice caring for over 24,000 patients. We value our staff, encourage learning and development, and recognise the important contribution every member of the team makes to providing safe, effective and compassionate patient care. The role will involve providing administrative support across a range of practice functions, with particular responsibility for coordinating safeguarding administration. This will include maintaining safeguarding records, monitoring actions and ensuring relevant information is accurately recorded and followed up. The postholder will be responsible for managing patient recalls and monitoring outstanding actions to ensure patients are invited for appropriate reviews and follow-up. They will also support clinical and administrative audits, including gathering information, updating records and monitoring progress against agreed actions. Other duties will include clinical and administrative coding, maintaining accurate patient information, processing correspondence, preparing reports and supporting the practice with routine data management. The role will also involve providing administrative support for practice meetings, including preparing agendas, taking minutes, recording decisions and maintaining action logs to ensure agreed actions are followed through. The successful candidate will need to be highly organised, methodical and able to manage their own workload, ensuring that important deadlines, reviews and follow-up actions are not missed. Confidentiality, accuracy and good attention to detail are essential. Main Purpose of the Role To provide comprehensive administrative support to the practice, with specific responsibility for safeguarding administration, patient recalls, clinical and administrative audits and maintaining accurate patient records. The postholder will support the smooth day-to-day running of the practice, working closely with clinical and non-clinical colleagues to ensure that administrative processes are completed accurately, efficiently and within agreed timescales. Act as the practice Safeguarding Administration Lead, providing administrative support to the clinical safeguarding leads. Maintain and update safeguarding registers and records for adults and children. Ensure safeguarding information and relevant documentation are accurately recorded and appropriately filed within patient records. Monitor safeguarding correspondence, referrals and incoming information, ensuring these are brought to the attention of the appropriate clinician. Maintain safeguarding action logs and monitor outstanding administrative actions. Support the organisation of safeguarding meetings and multidisciplinary discussions. Ensure relevant safeguarding documentation is processed and shared appropriately, in accordance with practice procedures and information governance requirements. Escalate any safeguarding concerns or urgent correspondence promptly to the appropriate clinical lead. Provide administrative support for the practice recall system. Identify and contact patients requiring reviews, investigations, monitoring or follow-up. Monitor outstanding recalls and maintain accurate records of invitations and patient responses. Follow up patients who have not responded to invitations in accordance with practice protocols. Support the monitoring of patients requiring regular reviews for long-term conditions and other clinical requirements. Assist with DNA (Did Not Attend) management, identifying missed appointments and supporting appropriate follow-up. Maintain accurate recall information and report any outstanding issues to the relevant clinical team. Lead and undertake practice audits as directed by the Practice Manager and clinical leads. Identify patients and gather relevant information for audit purposes. Extract, collate and accurately record data from clinical systems. Prepare audit reports and present findings where required. Maintain audit records and action plans, monitoring progress against agreed actions. Support the practice with clinical governance activities and quality improvement initiatives. Assist with the collection of evidence for enhanced services, contractual requirements and CQC compliance. Input relevant information into patient healthcare records accurately and in a timely manner. Undertake clinical coding of incoming correspondence, documents and other information in accordance with practice protocols and training. Process hospital letters, clinical correspondence and other patient documentation, ensuring information is directed appropriately. Maintain accurate patient demographic and registration information. Process new patient registrations, changes to patient details and deductions from the practice list. Support the maintenance of accurate patient records and undertake data quality checks as required. Provide administrative support for practice and multidisciplinary team meetings. Prepare meeting agendas and relevant documentation. Attend meetings as required and produce accurate minutes. Maintain meeting action logs, recording agreed actions, responsible individuals and timescales. Monitor outstanding actions and follow up with relevant colleagues. Provide general administrative and secretarial support to the clinical and management teams as required. Deal with patients and visitors both face to face and over the telephone in a professional, friendly and helpful manner. Welcome patients and visitors to the practice and direct enquiries to the appropriate team or service. Support the administration of the practice total triage system. Handle routine enquiries and pass clinical queries to the appropriate healthcare professional. Provide reception cover during periods of staff absence or increased demand. Support the opening and closing of the practice in accordance with the duty rota. Act as a chaperone when required, following appropriate training and practice procedures. Support the delivery of enhanced services and other practice requirements. Contribute to the effective running of the wider multidisciplinary team. Participate in local initiatives and projects to improve service delivery and patient care. Attend community events and support activities to promote the practice. Participate in shared learning, training and development opportunities. Complete all mandatory training and induction programmes. Maintain confidentiality and comply with data protection, information governance and practice policies. Understand and comply with current safeguarding legislation and practice procedures relating to children and adults. Follow all practice policies, procedures and protocols, including health and safety requirements. Undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role, as requested by the Practice Manager or partners.

description: The Patient Services Administrator is a key member of the Mayfield Medical Centre reception team and is often the first point of contact for patients, carers and other visitors. The post holder will provide a welcoming, professional and efficient reception service, helping patients access the most appropriate care in line with practice procedures and agreed care-navigation guidance. The role involves working across reception and telephone channels, responding to a range of patient queries, booking and managing appointments, handling administrative requests and supporting the wider clinical and practice team. The post holder must communicate calmly and sensitively, maintain confidentiality, use the practice clinical system accurately and recognise when a request needs to be passed to a clinician or senior colleague. Patient reception and customer service Telephone and electronic communication Appointments and care navigation Patient records and clinical system administration Repeat prescriptions and medication requests Results, correspondence and referrals Teamwork and day to day practice support Confidentiality, information governance and safety PERSONAL RESPONSIBILITIES Take responsibility for working within the limits of your knowledge, training and competence, seeking advice or escalating concerns when required. Treat all patients, carers, visitors and colleagues with dignity, respect and without discrimination. Contribute to a culture of continuous improvement by identifying ways to improve the patient experience and the effectiveness of reception processes. Adhere to Salus Medical Services and Mayfield Medical Centre policies, procedures and values. ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES The following are the core responsibilities of the Patient Services Administrator. The list is not exhaustive, and the post holder may be required to undertake other duties appropriate to the role, depending on service needs, workload and staffing levels. All duties must be carried out in accordance with practice policies, written protocols, training and the post holder's level of competence. Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, professional and courteous manner, establishing the reason for their visit where appropriate. Act as the first point of contact for patients attending the practice, helping them navigate the building and access the correct service or member of the team. Maintain an approachable and helpful manner while managing competing demands at the reception desk. Respond to patient queries sensitively, including when patients are distressed, anxious, frustrated or unhappy, and seek support from a senior colleague when needed. Maintain patient dignity and privacy when speaking with patients at the reception desk and take care not to disclose confidential information where others may overhear. Manage visitors, deliveries and other enquiries, directing them to the appropriate person or area. Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally, using the practice telephone system and agreed call-handling procedures. Establish the nature of each call, obtain and confirm relevant details, and direct or signpost the caller in line with practice protocols and care-navigation guidance. Handle appointment requests, prescription queries, test-result enquiries and general administrative questions within the limits of the role. Recognise calls that may require urgent clinical attention and follow the practice's escalation procedures without attempting to make clinical decisions. Record accurate messages, including the caller's name, contact details, reason for calling and any relevant urgency, and pass them to the appropriate person in a timely manner. Use approved methods to respond to patient communications, including online consultation requests, email or other digital channels where these form part of the practice workflow. Maintain a professional and considerate approach when dealing with difficult or challenging telephone conversations. Process requests for same-day and routine appointments received in person, by telephone and through approved digital routes. Book, amend and cancel appointments accurately, following appointment booking rules, clinician availability and practice protocols. Use the practice's care-navigation guidance to help patients access the most appropriate service or healthcare professional. Explain appointment options and relevant practice processes clearly, without providing clinical advice or making clinical assessments. Identify requests that fall outside standard booking guidance and refer them to the appropriate clinician or senior member of the team. Handle requests for home visits in accordance with practice procedures, recording the information required and passing the request to the appropriate clinician for assessment. Manage appointment changes and cancellations, including notifying relevant team members where necessary. Support the recall and follow-up of patients for appointments, reviews and other practice activity as directed. Use the practice clinical system and other relevant software confidently and accurately, maintaining up-to-date patient information. Register new patients in accordance with practice procedures, including checking registration information and completing the required data entry. Process patient amendments, including changes of name, address, telephone number and other demographic details, following identity and verification procedures. Retrieve and update patient records appropriately, ensuring information is entered accurately and in the correct place. Scan, attach, workflow and code incoming correspondence or documents in accordance with practice protocols and the post holder's training. Ensure messages, administrative actions and patient contacts are recorded clearly and passed to the correct workflow or team member. Maintain accurate records of actions taken and ensure outstanding tasks are managed or handed over appropriately. Receive and process repeat prescription requests in accordance with the practice's prescribing policy and agreed procedures. Check that requests contain the necessary information and are directed to the appropriate prescribing workflow. Direct medication queries, requests for acute medication and questions about medicines to the appropriate clinician or prescribing team. Explain the practice's prescription request and collection processes, including expected timescales, using approved information. Do not make changes to medication requests, provide medication advice or promise that a prescription will be issued; refer queries outside the administrative process to the appropriate person. Liaise with care homes to ensure their repeat prescriptions are processed appropriately. Handle enquiries about test results in line with practice protocols, ensuring that results requiring clinical interpretation are directed to an appropriate clinician. Do not interpret or communicate clinical results unless specifically authorised under an approved practice process and appropriate training. Process outgoing referrals and associated administrative information as directed, ensuring details are accurate and documentation is sent through the correct route. Receive, scan, workflow and distribute incoming clinical correspondence in accordance with practice procedures. Track administrative tasks and outstanding correspondence where required, escalating delays, missing information or urgent items to the appropriate team member. Provide patients with approved information about referral processes and direct clinical questions to the relevant healthcare professional. Teamwork and day-to-day practice support Work collaboratively with reception colleagues, GPs, nurses, pharmacists, allied health professionals and the wider practice team to support an effective patient service. Communicate relevant information to colleagues clearly and promptly, ensuring that patient requests are not missed or unnecessarily delayed. Support an effective handover between shifts and ensure outstanding work is appropriately recorded and handed over. Cover reception desks, telephone lines and other agreed administrative duties to maintain service resilience. Undertake routine administrative tasks that support the smooth running of the practice, including filing, photocopying, scanning and preparing documents. Support the organisation of clinics and the preparation of rooms or paperwork where required by the practice. Participate in team meetings, training and development activities relevant to the role. Maintain strict confidentiality in relation to patients, staff and practice business, and comply with data protection and information-governance requirements. Access patient records only where there is a legitimate work-related reason and follow the practice's policies for handling and sharing information. Follow safeguarding procedures and promptly pass on concerns about the safety or welfare of a child or adult at risk to the designated person, in line with training and policy. Follow health and safety, infection prevention and control, fire safety and security procedures. Maintain a safe and tidy reception and working environment, reporting hazards, incidents, near misses or equipment faults. Follow procedures for opening and closing the building, including the safe use of keys, doors, windows and alarm systems where this forms part of the shift. Complete all mandatory training and keep knowledge of practice procedures up to date. Other duties Assist with maintaining a clean, tidy and welcoming reception and waiting room environment, reporting any cleaning or maintenance issues. Undertake reasonable additional administrative and reception duties appropriate to the level and scope of the post, as requested by the Practice Manager or delegated manager. Work flexibly to support the needs of the practice, including providing cover across reception positions when required.

Monitoring actions, deadlines and outstanding information, liaising with relevant colleagues to support timely completion. Communicating professionally with Trust colleagues, contractors, suppliers and other stakeholders on behalf of the Associate Director and wider team. Manage the Associate Directors diary, arrange meetings and appointments, coordinate meeting requirements and ensure relevant information and documentation are available when required. Maintain SharePoint folders and electronic filing systems, ensuring documents are appropriately named, organised, version-controlled and easily accessible to authorised members of the team. Maintain and update project trackers, programme information, action logs, databases and other Estates records, ensuring information remains accurate and current. Prepare and format correspondence, reports, presentations, briefings, spreadsheets and meeting papers to a professional standard. Provide administrative support for meetings, including preparation and circulation of agendas and papers, taking accurate minutes and maintaining records of decisions and agreed actions. Monitor actions, deadlines and outstanding information arising from meetings and project activities, following up with relevant colleagues as required.

You will receive, assist, and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. You will provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. You will have excellent communication skills, a compassionate and friendly nature who can operate in a busy environment with a range of people and professions, as you will be working with our clinical and administration teams. This role is ideal for someone who is highly organised and an effective communicator who can provide a professional and warm welcome to our patients, ensuring every contact is of the highest quality. Deal sensitively with patients who may be anxious, distressed, frustrated or experiencing difficult personal circumstances. Maintain a clean, organised and welcoming reception and waiting area. Manage challenging situations professionally and escalate complaints or concerns to the appropriate member of the practice team. Care Navigation and Appointment Management Handle patient requests for appointments, advice and access to healthcare services by telephone and in person. Use approved care navigation protocols to direct patients to the most appropriate clinician or service, including GPs, practice nurses, clinical pharmacists, physiotherapists and other available services where appropriate. Gather relevant non-clinical information to help determine the appropriate appointment pathway, without attempting to diagnose medical conditions. Book, amend and cancel appointments using the practices clinical computer system. Identify potentially urgent concerns in accordance with practice procedures and promptly escalate them to a clinician. Provide information about alternative services, such as NHS 111, where appropriate and in accordance with practice guidance. Maintain accurate records of patient contacts and appointment requests. Telephone and Administrative Duties Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and manage a busy call queue efficiently. Handle patient messages and ensure they are passed to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice policies and direct medication queries to the appropriate professional. Register new patients and update demographic details, contact information and other relevant records. Manage incoming and outgoing post, emails and electronic communications. Assist with administrative tasks, including recalling patients for appointments, supporting clinical audits and maintaining accurate practice records. Monitor outstanding administrative tasks and follow up requests within agreed timescales. Clinical Systems and Data Management Use the practices electronic clinical system, SystmOne, to access and update patient information. Ensure patient details, appointment information and messages are recorded accurately and promptly. Handle sensitive patient information securely and maintain strict confidentiality at all times. Comply with UK GDPR, data protection legislation, information governance requirements and practice policies. Follow procedures for accessing, storing and sharing patient information appropriately. Teamwork and Practice Support Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, pharmacists, care coordinators and administrative colleagues. Attend staff meetings and training sessions as required. Support colleagues during busy periods and assist with the day-to-day organisation of reception services. Follow practice policies relating to health and safety, infection prevention, safeguarding and equality and diversity. Report incidents, risks and concerns to the appropriate manager. Undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role to support the effective operation of the practice. Training and Development The successful candidate will receive induction and training appropriate to the role, including practice procedures, clinical systems, information governance, confidentiality, safeguarding, health and safety and care navigation. Ongoing training and development will be encouraged to support the delivery of a safe, efficient and high-quality patient service. Personal Qualities We are looking for someone who is approachable, empathetic, dependable and proactive. The successful candidate must demonstrate patience, discretion and professionalism when dealing with sensitive situations and be committed to treating every patient with dignity, respect and fairness. Working Conditions The postholder will work within a busy GP practice and may be required to work flexibly according to the needs of the service. Working hours, salary, annual leave and other employment terms will be confirmed during recruitment.

You will help reduce unnecessary GP workload while recognising when something is outside your remit and needs to be escalated. Day-to-day work may include reviewing hospital letters, investigation results and other clinical correspondence, extracting and coding relevant information, updating patient records, filing documentation and directing tasks to the appropriate team. You may also support note summarising and other activities that maintain clear, accurate clinical records. Accuracy and patient safety are at the heart of this role. You will need to manage your workload, follow practice and national guidance, and know when to seek advice from a GP, supervisor or manager. By ensuring clinical information is handled accurately, promptly and safely, you will help our clinicians work effectively and support patient care. Your main duties will include processing incoming clinical correspondence, accurately updating patient records, reviewing and coding clinical information, and ensuring information is directed to the appropriate team member. You will support the processing of hospital and clinic letters, results, safeguarding information and electronic data, as well as summarising new patient records, supporting registrations and managing out-of-area correspondence.
